extra.message: SQL Injection in Student.create — Attacker-controlled arbitrary SQL execution against Postgres — read/modify/delete any data, bypass authentication, potentially escalate to RCE via DB extensions [verified: Student.create builds the INSERT via Python % formatting directly into the SQL string with no parameterization or escaping, and views.py passes POST body data['name'] straight into it, so a value containing a quote breaks out of the literal for full SQL injection.]

Unauthenticated/unauthorized grade assignment via evaluate endpoint — Any unauthenticated or non-admin user can assign arbitrary grades (marks) to any student for any course, bypassing the admin-only UI restriction entirely — full grade-integrity compromise [verified: evaluate() at views.py:135-153 has no @authorize()/admin check; EVALUATE_SCHEMA only validates points range, and the admin-only gating in course.jinja2 is UI-only, so any unauthenticated request can insert Mark records.]

CSRF protection disabled application-wide — An attacker can craft a malicious page that submits forged POST requests (create students/courses, submit grades, post reviews, log a victim in/out) on behalf of an authenticated victim's browser session, since no CSRF token is enforced. [verified: csrf_middleware is defined but commented out of the middlewares list at app.py:27, so no CSRF token validation occurs on any state-changing endpoint.]

Stored XSS via disabled autoescaping and unescaped review/course fields — Stored cross-site scripting: any user who creates a course or submits a course review can inject JavaScript that executes in the browser of every other user who views that course page, enabling session/cookie theft, CSRF-token theft, or full account takeover. [verified: autoescape=False at app.py:35 disables Jinja2 auto-escaping globally, and templates render course/review fields without |e; combined with unvalidated review_text storage, persistent JS injection is possible.]

Missing authentication/authorization on state-changing routes — Unauthenticated attackers can create arbitrary students/courses, assign grades to any student for any course, and post arbitrary review content — full write access to core business data without logging in. [verified: grep of views.py confirms students, student, courses, course, review, and evaluate view functions all lack any @authorize() decorator while only logout has one, so /students/ and /courses/ create/list and evaluate/review POSTs are reachable without authentication.]

Missing authentication/authorization on student creation and listing — Any anonymous visitor can create student records or enumerate all students/marks, exposing PII and enabling data pollution [verified: students() handler at views.py:52-57 has no @authorize() decorator, unlike logout(); any anonymous POST creates a Student record.]

Unauthenticated course creation — Any anonymous user can create arbitrary courses, polluting application data and enabling stored XSS payloads via title/description fields rendered later in course.jinja2/courses.jinja2 templates without an authenticated session. [verified: courses() handler at views.py:86-90 has no @authorize() decorator and no auth_user check, so any anonymous POST creates arbitrary courses.]

Potential stored XSS via review_text/course/student fields — If templates render these fields unescaped, an attacker-submitted review or course description executes JavaScript in other users' (including admin) sessions, enabling session theft [verified: app.py:35 sets autoescape=False globally for Jinja2, and review_text/title/description are inserted into templates via Review.create/Course.create with no sanitization, so unauthenticated stored XSS is confirmed.]

Weak password hashing (unsalted MD5) — If the users table is ever exfiltrated (e.g. via the SQL injection above), all passwords can be cracked instantly with precomputed tables [verified: user.py:41 shows check_password comparing pwd_hash to unsalted md5(password), with no salt/pepper anywhere in the User model or DAO, so a leaked users table (e.g. via SQLi) is trivially crackable with rainbow tables.]

Insecure session cookie flags (HttpOnly disabled) — Any reflected/stored XSS on the site can steal the session cookie directly via document.cookie, leading to full account takeover [verified: middlewares.py:20 explicitly sets httponly=False on RedisStorage, an insecure config genuinely present on the session cookie carrying user_id, and no Secure/SameSite override is present either.]

Session cookie missing HttpOnly flag — Combined with the stored XSS above, JavaScript injected via a review/course field can read the session cookie directly via `document.cookie`, allowing session hijacking and account takeover. [verified: Confirmed same line: RedisStorage(app['redis'], httponly=False) disables HttpOnly on the session cookie, a real missing-control issue independent of any XSS chain.]

Debug mode enabled — Verbose error pages/tracebacks may leak internal application state, file paths, and stack details to attackers probing for errors (e.g. via malformed input to the SQLi-prone endpoints). [verified: Application(debug=True) at app.py:24 enables verbose tracebacks on unhandled errors in what is configured as the shipped app; genuine misconfiguration though lower severity than XSS/CSRF.]
